title: Immutable-reference-suite-checkin-protocol-and-audit-ledger
creator: Ava Chen
description: Establish a disciplined check-in protocol for the canonical reference-suite (golden dataset) used by automated evals. The goal is to make every mutation to the reference suite auditable, reversible, and gated so that config or model changes always trigger appropriate regressions runs and human review before rollout. This covers signing immutable snapshots, attaching change metadata (author, rationale, linked PRs), enforcing fine-grained ACLs for edits, and wiring CI/CD to block config/model rollouts until regression thresholds pass.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable snapshot workflow exists: maintainers can create an immutable snapshot of reference suite with signature and metadata.
Every snapshot is recorded in an access ledger with timestamp, author, rationale, and linked artifacts (PRs, dashboards).
Config and model changes in CI trigger an automated re-eval against the latest approved snapshot; failures block the rollout.
Role-based ACLs enforced: only designated stewards can approve snapshot promotions; edits must be staged and logged.
Rollback playbook documented and testable: revert to prior snapshot with audit trail and re-run evals.
tasks: Design snapshot schema and signature format (S3 path + content-hash + signer) - XFN review
Implement signature and immutability enforcement on storage (S3/GCS policy + lambda check)
Build access ledger service (append-only manifest) and UI for recent snapshots
Integrate CI hooks: capture config/model hashes, trigger eval job, surface pass/fail in PR
Create steward workflow for staging -> approval -> promotion and ACL rules
Author rollback playbook and conduct incident tabletop exercise

notes: Avoid coupling this protocol tightly to a single storage vendor; design for pluggable backends. Keep the steward role narrow: approve/promote snapshots only. CI gating should be configurable per-service to avoid blocking low-risk maintenance patches.
owner_rotation_plan: Rotation every 6 months; steward list stored in SSO group 'golden-stewards@redwood.com' and reviewed quarterly.
retention_policy: Keep last 50 promoted snapshots; archive older snapshots to cold storage with preserved signature records.
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose regressed evals as paged incidents if customer-impacting or failure persists across two consecutive promoted snapshots; dashboard for snapshot health and eval pass rates.
risks: High operational friction if sign-off process is too heavyweight — may slow velocity.
Mis-signed snapshots could lead to distrust in gate decisions; requires strong KMS controls.
Incomplete CI coverage could allow regressions to slip through if some services skip gating.
